dedupe_keys.name: rocket emissions impact dataset 2019 launch and re entry inventory with geos chem results ucl

description: This dataset holds a global inventory of rocket launch emissions for 2019 and the atmospheric chemistry results built on it. An Excel spreadsheet itemises each 2019 launch by location, time, fuel type and the emissions of each stage, together with the time and location of re-entries of space debris, reusable rocket parts and discarded launch hardware. NetCDF files give GEOS-Chem (v12.9.7) simulation results for radiative forcing and changes in species concentrations after a decade of emissions growth and under a space tourism scenario, expressed as the difference between runs with and without rocket emissions. It was compiled by Robert Ryan and Eloise Marais of UCL with European Research Council funding, and is downloadable from the UCL Research Data Repository (about 183 MB) under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: the inventory covers one year, per-stage emissions are estimated from vehicle user manuals, not measured, and results depend on the chemical transport model set-up. It supports environmental-impact assessment of launch activity and scenarios for the growth of space infrastructure; a related record is the 2020 to 2022 megaconstellation-era launch and re-entry emissions inventory.
